headline_marked: [[Iran missile attack hits 2 UAE oil tankers]] in Strait of Hormuz, 1 sailor killed
headline: Iran missile attack hits 2 UAE oil tankers in Strait of Hormuz, 1 sailor killed
summary: One Indian sailor was killed and eight others, including six Indians and two Ukrainians, were injured after missiles struck two UAE oil tankers in Omani waters. The attack sparked fires on both vessels, which were later brought under control.
details: The UAE Ministry of Defense claims Iranian missiles struck two of its oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in one Indian sailor killed and eight others injured. Six of the injured are Indian nationals, and two are Ukrainian.
The incident occurred on Tuesday, July 14, when the tankers, named Al-Bahiya and Mombasa, were in Oman's regional waters. The deceased Indian sailor was working on the Mombasa tanker.

Following the missile impact, both vessels caught fire. However, the UAE Ministry of Defense stated that the fires were subsequently brought under control. Details regarding the current condition of the damaged tankers or their safe removal have not been disclosed.

The UAE Ministry of Defense has declared a state of heightened alert regarding the security situation, vowing to counter any threats to the nation's security and stability. They also warned that all necessary measures would be taken against any attempts to disrupt state security.

In a separate statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the attack. Abu Dhabi expressed deep condolences to the family of the deceased Indian sailor and extended solidarity to New Delhi.

The Foreign Ministry characterized obstructing commercial shipping and using the Strait of Hormuz for political pressure or economic blackmail as acts of piracy. Such actions, they stated, not only threaten regional stability but also global energy security.

The Strait of Hormuz is a vital waterway through which a significant volume of crude oil and fuel products is transported daily. Any military attack or escalation in this passage could have immediate repercussions on international energy markets, global trade, and regional security, potentially deepening existing Middle East tensions.

headline_marked: [[Deal with Iran still possible]], says Trump despite new attacks and sanctions
headline: Deal with Iran still possible, says Trump despite new attacks and sanctions
summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a deal with Tehran to end the conflict remains possible, even after recent attacks and the re-imposition of naval blockades on Iranian ports. He claimed a deal was almost reached just two days prior.
details: US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that a deal with Tehran to end the conflict remains possible. This assertion comes despite renewed attacks on Iran and the re-imposition of naval blockades on its ports.
Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office at the White House, Trump confidently said, "Yes, I think a deal is possible. I certainly do." He emphasized his belief in the potential for a resolution.
Trump further revealed that "we had a deal with them just two days ago." However, he added, "But then they said, 'Oh, we can't do this deal. We have to discuss it further.'"

Earlier on Monday, amidst reciprocal missile and drone attacks between the two nations, Trump announced the re-implementation of sanctions on Iran. He claimed the US would take responsibility for the security of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a telephone interview with Fox News today, Trump asserted, "We're going to control the Strait of Hormuz. We're probably going to operate it. We're going to be the guardian of the strait. We should be paid for it."

Trump argued that the US should receive "a lot of money" for undertaking this responsibility. He reasoned that the countries using this waterway are wealthy and should not expect this service from the US for free.
